title: Test cheaper models on tasks your agent once failed
summary: Helena Tan turned 23 failures from building a web app with Claude Code into a test set; she reports cheaper models solved many tasks at a fraction of the cost.
model: Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Haiku 4.5
agent_role: Coding agents ran each of the 23 tasks three times in the same setup; programmatic checks and an AI judge scored the results. The author designed the tasks, answer keys and checked the judge against human labels.
outcome: Her leaderboard shows Haiku 4.5 passing about 55% at roughly $0.32 per solved task versus about 90% at roughly $1.9 for the top models, with overlapping error margins.
what_they_did: The author built a full web app with Claude Code on the priciest model and kept running out of credits. She turned each failure she hit into a test task, 23 in total, covering vague requests, long multi-step rules, full builds and data with hidden traps. Then she ran six Claude models on all of them, three times each.
how_it_went: Her published results show the newer top models solving 21 of 23 tasks on the first try, mid-tier ones close behind, and the budget model 13. She says the margins are too small to call a clear winner.
worth_knowing: Every model struggled when asked something vague: most built without asking questions. She also says 12 of 23 tasks came out the same on all models, so only 11 actually separate them.
prompt: Help me build a small personal test set for choosing a cheaper model. Here are [number] problems my coding agent got wrong while building [project]: [list]. For each, write a short task, the starting files or data, and a clear answer key for what counts as correct. Then propose how to run each task three times on [models to compare] and record pass rate and cost. Show me the task list and plan before running anything that spends credits.

curation.rationale: A benchmark, but grounded in a concrete personal need: turning real failures from building an app into tasks to see if cheaper models can do the job. Detailed public results; the workflow is more evaluation than delegation.
